reasoning_traces.think:
The core mechanism involves perceptual expectation formation from sensory cues, particularly in goal- and means-object contexts. In maze environments, animals develop expectations about spatial layout and object properties. When these expectations are violated—through manipulation of goal-object characteristics—the resulting behavioral disruption indicates a failure in prior belief alignment. This process maps to Bayesian inference where prior beliefs (expectations) are updated with likelihoods derived from sensory input. If the likelihood does not match the prior, a posterior update fails, manifesting as disruption. The GSE layer models this as a state transition triggered by stimulus-character mismatch. The dual nature of this system lies in its ability to predict and react to deviations, forming a closed-loop perception-action cycle. Failure modes include overconfidence in expectation, insufficient sensory resolution, or lack of adaptive mechanisms to revise beliefs.
